clue.text: Dorothy returned having had dinner already

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the short name is read backwards

parts.note: Dot is a short form of the name Dorothy
had dinner means ate

explanation.surface: Someone notes that Dorothy came home having already eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'to date' means up to now, so it can stand for 'already' in many sentences.

clue.text: Experimental container base set up to north of Spain

indicators.note: in a down entry, being north of something means being placed above it
in a down clue, set up means the letters are written climbing the grid, bottom to top

parts.note: a butt is the thick base end of something, such as a rifle
set is taken as itself, a synonym of the word 'set' in its own sense
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Instructions for an experiment: set a container on a base and position it above something Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BUTT and SET together, giving TESTTUB, and 'to north of' places that above E.
explanation.definitionFit: A test tube is the small glass vessel used for laboratory experiments.

clue.text: Vicious introductory statement to girl possibly brought up in termination of contract

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up means writing it from the bottom upwards
to joins one piece onto the other, the statement being attached to the girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl, the 'possibly' marking this as one example
Sid Vicious of the Sex Pistols would introduce himself with 'I'm Sid'

explanation.surface: A cruel opening remark to a young woman gets mentioned when someone's contract is ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vicious' is not an adjective but the punk Sid Vicious, whose self-introduction would be I'M SID; 'brought up' reverses LASS plus IMSID.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismissal is being fired, the ending of an employment contract by the employer.

clue.text: Broken nut with end missing and second-rate washer

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so these letters are put back together in a new order
with its end missing, the last letter of the word with is dropped

parts.note: B is the grade below A, so second-rate gives B

explanation.surface: A cracked nut and a missing end make for a poor-quality washer, as on a bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end missing' takes H off WITH to leave WIT, and 'Broken' mixes NUT and WIT into TWINTU.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-tub is an old-style washing machine with separate tubs for washing and spinning.

clue.text: Prince, in grip of frenzied love, turned musical

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the whole assembly is read backwards
being in the grip of something means being held inside it

parts.note: running amok is being frenzied, out of control
Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
love means zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A prince, gripped by mad love, became the subject of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the whole assembly, giving AMOHALKO before reversal; 'Prince' suggests Prince the singer, but is Shakespeare's Prince Hal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is the famous Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show.

clue.text: Clip inside edge, getting ahead of Aussies — they're pants

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting ahead of means coming first, above the next piece
inside means one word is set within the other

parts.note: a kerb is the edge of a pavement
to clip or nick is to cut slightly
ocker is Australian slang for an uncouth Australian man

explanation.surface: A sports report: catching the inside edge puts one side ahead of the Australians, who are dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish, which suits the surface, but here it means trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickerbockers are loose breeches gathered at the knee, so they are a kind of trousers.

clue.text: This area, in sum, got stuck

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to sum is to add
here means this place or area

explanation.surface: Someone working a sum in this part of the page got stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast, so the past tense means stuck to something.

clue.text: Best open event

parts.note: something out in the open is public, so out can mean open
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: An advertisement for the finest open-air event of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat or surpass them, the verb sense of 'best'.

clue.text: Sportsman who uses landline rather than net?

definitions.text: Sportsman who uses landline rather than net?

parts.words: Sportsman who uses landline rather than net?
parts.note: the surface is about telephones and the internet, but the fisherman casts a line onto water from the land instead of trawling with a net

explanation.surface: Someone sporty prefers the old house telephone to going online.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod fisherman uses hook and line, not a net, often fishing from the bank.

clue.text: Unhealthy ingredient in tart regularly ruined fantastic day

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word tart
ruined means wrecked, so these letters are rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: A baker's lament: something bad for you in the tart spoiled a wonderful day.
explanation.definitionFit: Trans fats are a type of fat in processed food linked to heart disease, hence unhealthy.

clue.text: Dish combining two starters from one branch of Islam and three from another

indicators.note: keeping only the two opening letters means the rest of the word is dropped

parts.note: Sunni is the larger branch of Islam

indicators.note: keeping three letters from the start means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: another branch of Islam is Shia

explanation.surface: A meal mixing the cooking of two different Muslim traditions.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep SU of SUNNI and SHI of SHIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese food of vinegared rice with raw fish, a dish.

clue.text: Loaded lads' gathering outside East German house

indicators.note: outside means the first word goes around the next piece

parts.note: loaded is slang for very wealthy
E is the compass abbreviation for east
a stag is a men-only party before a wedding

explanation.surface: A drunken bachelor party gathers outside a building in eastern Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reichstag is the building in Berlin housing the German parliament.

clue.text: Knight heading west time after time, an Arthurian

indicators.note: after means the earlier piece follows the later one
in an across entry, heading west means running right to left

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: A knight riding west again and again, one of King Arthur's men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading west' gives RIS; 'after' puts the second time first, so the second T comes before RIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristan was one of the Knights of the Round Table, lover of Isolde.

clue.text: Knock back knockout toddy to get energy for public performance

indicators.note: knock back means drink, but here sends the letters backwards

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for knockout
arak is a spirit distilled from palm toddy
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Downing a strong toddy gives the courage to sing in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' reverses KO plus ARAK, giving KARAOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke is amateur singing to a backing track in front of others in a bar.

clue.text: Put smart clothes on ahead of rendezvous — that shows things haven't gone stale!

definitions.text: that shows things haven't gone stale!

parts.note: putting on your Sunday best is dressing in smart clothes
ahead of means before
a rendezvous is a meeting, a date

explanation.surface: Advice to dress up before a romantic meeting, so you don't look tired.
explanation.definitionFit: The label on food packs gives the day up to which it stays fresh.

clue.text: Pre-med perhaps given before operations — upon which they are carried out?

definitions.text: upon which they are carried out?

indicators.note: in a down entry, given before means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a pre-med, a sedative before surgery, may be given as a tablet
ops is short for operations

explanation.surface: A sedative is given before surgery, on the tables where surgery happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they' refers back to operations, which may be done on table surfaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabletops are the flat upper surfaces of tables, on which work or surgery can be done.

clue.text: E.g. McDonald's cheese more than half squashed

parts.note: a McDonald is a typical Scottish surname, so one example is a Scot

indicators.note: keeping more than half of the word means its last three letters are dropped

parts.note: cheddar is a cheese

explanation.surface: A fast-food chain's cheese, mostly flattened.
explanation.walkthrough: McDonald's suggests the burger chain, but a McDonald is a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to crush it, so a quashed idea has been squashed.

clue.text: Santa's close to ring covering stove-top — how must he feel in that chimney!

definitions.text: how must he feel in that chimney!

indicators.note: close to means placed right beside the following piece

parts.note: Santa is Santa Claus

indicators.note: covering means the ring goes around the next piece

parts.note: a tropic is a circle of latitude around the earth
a hob is the top surface of a stove

explanation.surface: Father Christmas squeezed past the cooker ring into a narrow chimney: how cramped he must feel!
explanation.definitionFit: Claustrophobia is fear of tight enclosed spaces, which a narrow flue would provoke.

clue.text: Free French articles on foolish resistance lost

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: un and le are French articles, indefinite and definite

indicators.note: lost means a letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: rash means foolish or reckless
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Free French newspaper articles about futile resistance being defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free French' suggests the wartime movement; 'Free' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash a dog is to let it off the lead, setting it free.

clue.text: Wellington may be reinforced here — he's right outside Napoleon's base

indicators.note: outside means the outer pieces go round the next one

parts.note: he is taken as itself, the 's acting as a link
Elba was the island where Napoleon was exiled in 1814

explanation.surface: The Duke of Wellington has the upper hand over Napoleon at his island base.
explanation.walkthrough: A wellington is also a rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel bar is a quick shoe-repair counter, where a boot's heel can be fixed.

clue.text: French drink wine in addition

indicators.note: in means the wine goes inside the other piece

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an addition at the end of a letter
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A French drink with wine added.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastis is an aniseed-flavoured aperitif from the south of France.

clue.text: Gold price recovery reported

definitions.note: the definition is a participle, standing in for the adverb sense of heard by ear

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a rally is a recovery in market prices

explanation.surface: A financial bulletin says the price of gold is bouncing back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something received by ear has been heard, as a reported item is conveyed through speech.

clue.text: Get ready to produce rent before getting space

indicators.note: in a down entry, before means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a rent is a rip or tear
an en is a printer's space, half an em

explanation.surface: Preparing to pay the rent before moving into a space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like payment but is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to become mature, as fruit gets ready to eat.

clue.text: Extremely fine art expressing grief?

definitions.meaning: the superlative of keen in the sense sharp, the sharpest edge
in old English, thou ... is the form for 'thou art keening', wailing in mourning

explanation.definitionFit: Keen means sharp or fine-edged, and to keen is to wail for the dead in Irish tradition.

clue.text: Performer can depart flamboyantly

indicators.note: doing something flamboyantly means with showy flourishes, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An entertainer is able to make a showy exit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap-dancer is a stage artiste who dances in shoes with metal plates.

clue.text: There's nothing between the two where voter marks cross

indicators.note: being between means the nought sits inside the other word

parts.note: both means the two of them
O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: No difference between the two candidates, so the voter spoils the ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: A polling booth is the cubicle where an elector puts an X on a ballot paper.

clue.text: Has nudes developed, giving protection from light

indicators.note: developed in a photographic sense, so these letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has nude photos printed, which must be kept out of the light.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol or awning keeps the sun off, shading from bright rays.

clue.text: 'Highly commended' one sacked, forced out

indicators.note: sacked means dismissed, so one letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: highly commended means praised
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: An employee once highly praised has been fired and pushed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To prise something is to lever it open or out by force.
